cases.name: Ariel Cae Jones
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She had a special bond with her great-great aunt and uncle, Emma Robinson and the late Odell Robinson. They were considered her second parents.

Ariel attended Warren Township School System in Indianapolis, Indiana. She later attended Parker High School in Birmingham, Alabama. She was baptized in her early youth at Rose Christian Church where she was a member for many years during her childhood.

Ariel enjoyed singing and dancing. She was the life of the party. Her smile and goofy personality would light up a room. Ariel enjoyed spending time with her family and friends. Special times for her were the holidays and her birthday. Ariel loved getting her hair and nails done. She also had a passion for helping others feel and look their best.

Ariel loved her nephews and nieces like they were her own. She was the “fun Tee-Tee.” Ariel’s real child was her dog, “Elvis Jones” who she loved dearly."
cases.narrative: On 4/18/2023, her burned body was found inside a vehicle in the 8400 Block of 5th Avenue North in Birmingham, AL. An autopsy revealed she had been shot.

cases.name: Jermiera Ivory Fowler
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Her spirit was as vibrant as the city she called home.



Jermiera, having been the oldest of eight siblings, had a natural gift for leadership and a heart full of love. She was the kind of person who made everyone feel welcome and included, and her infectious energy and joy was contagious. Jermiera was an

entrepreneur and a motivational speaker, inspiring others to follow their dreams and live life to the fullest. Her wisdom and guidance helped countless people find their way, and her legacy will live on through the lives she touched.



Jermiera’s commitment to the Lord was the foundation of her life, and her baptism in 2006 was a testament to her faith and love for God. She lived her life with grace, compassion, and a deep sense of purpose, always striving to make the world a better place.



Jermiera was a devoted mother to her beautiful children, Paris and Levi, who were the light of her life. She was a loving sister, a loyal friend, and a role model to all who knew her. As we say goodbye to Jermiera, let us celebrate her life and her legacy. Let us honor her memory by living each day with the same passion, love, and joy that she brought to our lives. Rest in peace, dear Jermiera. You will always be remembered and cherished."
cases.narrative: On 6/1/2023, East Precinct officers discovered her burned body in the 1000 Block of Sellers Road in Birmingham, AL. An autopsy revealed she had been shot. She had visible signs of trauma and had been reported missing on June 1 after having not been seen nor heard from since the day before.
